title: Pro-étale inverse image preserves K-flat internal module complexes
statement: For every morphism f:X to Y of schemes and commutative ring object R [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] in abelian sheaves on Y_proet, the module transport [sk-def-sfb-transport] mapMod(f*) along the strong monoidal pullback [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] preserves unbounded K-flat complexes [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] of internal R-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], for their relative tensor product [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor].

source.place: Tags 0DEN and 0DEP, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks and lemma-pullback-K-flat-points; identity coefficient comparison case

proof.text: Let R be the arbitrary given commutative ring object and put S=f*R. The exact internal/section module equivalences identify signed total tensor and acyclicity by lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison. The acyclic-tensor characterization of K-flatness in lem-sfb-exact-monoidal-equivalence-total-kflat therefore identifies upstream quasi-isomorphism K-flatness with IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients after the section equivalence.

Apply lem-c2-proetale-section-module-algebraic-inverse-image to R, S=f*R and rho=id. It supplies the algebraic presentation whose module functor is naturally isomorphic to E_R.inverse followed by mapMod(f*) followed by E_S; comap(id) is naturally isomorphic to the identity. Whisker with E_R and use its unit isomorphism to obtain E_R followed by I.modules isomorphic to mapMod(f*) followed by E_S. This is the actual existing canonical strong pullback, with its ring and scalar actions.

The scheme-induced inverse image and direct image form a geometric morphism. Choose the conservative set-indexed family of target topos points from lem-sfb-proetale-enough-points and their RingedSitePoint presentations. Apply lem-sfb-algebraic-inverse-image-kflat to the section image of P. This proves its algebraic inverse image K-flat. Transport along the termwise natural comparison of step 2, then reflect K-flatness by step 1.
